newsitem.title: CHILE: Communist's arrest seen tarnishing Chile's image.
newsitem.headline: Communist's arrest seen tarnishing Chile's image.

text.p: The arrest of the Communist Party chief over allegedly slanderous statements she made about former ruler Augusto Pinochet will damage Chile's reputation abroad, the foreign minister said on Wednesday.

With Communist Party President Gladys Marin languishing in a detention centre, Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said her arrest on Tuesday would tarnish Chile's image only 10 days before a summit meeting in Santiago.

"Unfortunately, we're going to have a negative international repercussion because of this, I can't deny it," Insulza told reporters. "But this case is before the courts and the government must respect that."

Police arrested Marin on a judge's orders on charges she slandered the former military ruler, calling him a psychopath and a blackmailer at a memorial service for the 3,200 people, including Marin's husband, killed during Pinochet's rule.

The arrest, which made headlines in Chile and abroad, occurred 10 days before about 20 foreign heads of state arrive for an Ibero-American summit meeting, the biggest international event in Chile's history.

Leaders of President Eduardo Frei's government blasted the detention, calling it the work of an over-eager judge acting under pressure from Pinochet's lawyers. One senator called the arrest illegal and said the judge should be tried instead.
"This is unacceptable in a democracy. What Gladys Marin did was express a political opinion," Public Works Minister Ricardo Lagos said.

At the memorial service, Marin said Pinochet came to power through "scheming, treason and murder," referring to the 1973 coup. Pinochet, 80, remains commander-in-chief of the army although he ceded the presidency to civilians in 1990.
